blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At senior level, the balance sheet is no longer just a snapshot — it is a picture of the company's strategic position at a single moment, capturing decisions made over many years. The shape of the asset side reveals what the business invested in; the shape of the liabilities reveals how it financed those investments; and the size and growth of equity reveal the company's self-funding discipline.

A senior reader learns to ask structural questions rather than size questions. How liquid are the assets? How short is the debt? How much of the equity represents retained earnings, and how much represents fresh capital the owners had to put in simply to stay alive? Each answer says something about the quiet health of the business beneath the quarterly headlines.

The balance sheet is the slowest-changing document in accounting, and for that very reason often the most revealing. It is where strategy, discipline, and history all sit in a single page of numbers.

items.q: According to the text, what does the shape of the liabilities reveal?
options: What the business invested in
The liquidity of the assets
The company's self-funding discipline
How the business financed its investments
items.why: "The shape of the liabilities reveals how it financed those investments."

items.q: What kind of questions does a senior reader learn to ask?
options: Structural questions
Questions about the audit
Size questions
Questions about the quarterly headlines
items.why: "A senior reader learns to ask structural questions rather than size questions."

items.q: Why does the author call the balance sheet "often the most revealing"?
options: Because it is the slowest-changing document
Because it is prepared by the board
Because it is the largest document in accounting
Because it is audited most frequently
items.why: "the slowest-changing document in accounting, and for that very reason often the most revealing."

items.q: The distinction between retained earnings and fresh capital suggests that the author…
options: regards all equity as equally healthy
sees equity built from profits as a healthier sign than capital injected to survive
believes fresh capital is always preferable
thinks equity is irrelevant to strategy
items.why: Inferência: "fresh capital the owners had to put in simply to stay alive" carrega tom de fragilidade, ao contrário dos lucros retidos.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: The quarterly headlines tell you more than the balance sheet does.
Slow-moving numbers can be highly informative.
How the debt is structured matters, not only how much there is.
A balance sheet can express years of strategic decisions.
items.why: Inferência: o texto valoriza a "saúde silenciosa" sob as manchetes trimestrais — o oposto de confiar mais nas manchetes.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie orientando um novo membro do conselho. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Look at these three companies side by side. If you only read the P&L, you would swear they were almost identical — same revenue, comparable margins, similar profit. But turn to the balance sheet and the resemblance falls apart completely.

The first one funds itself. Almost all of its equity is retained earnings, built up quietly year after year. It carries very little debt, and what it does carry is long-dated. That is a business that can survive a bad year without asking anyone for permission.

The second looks profitable, but the equity is mostly fresh capital the owners injected eighteen months ago to keep the doors open. The debt is short and it reprices constantly. On paper it thrives; underneath, it is fragile.

The third has hoarded cash and let its assets go stale — liquid, yes, but nobody is reinvesting. That is not strength; that is a board with no idea what to do next.

So before you vote on anything tonight, ask me the structural questions. How liquid, how short, how self-funded. The numbers on the surface will never tell you that.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why does Sophie say the three companies look almost identical at first?
options: They belong to the same holding group
They share the same auditor
Their P&Ls show similar revenue, margins and profit
Their balance sheets match
items.why: "If you only read the P&L… same revenue, comparable margins, similar profit."

items.q: What makes the first company resilient, according to Sophie?
options: It has sold most of its assets
It holds a large amount of short-term debt
Its equity is mostly retained earnings and its debt is long-dated
It has just raised fresh capital
items.why: "Almost all of its equity is retained earnings… what it does carry is long-dated."

items.q: What does Sophie imply about the second company?
options: Its apparent profitability hides a fragile financial structure
It carries no debt at all
It is the strongest of the three
It is about to be acquired
items.why: Inferência: "On paper it thrives; underneath, it is fragile" — a lucratividade aparente esconde a fragilidade.

items.q: Why is the third company's pile of cash NOT a sign of strength?
options: Because the board is not reinvesting or acting on it
Because the cash is illiquid
Because it will be taxed heavily
Because it was borrowed at a high rate
items.why: "nobody is reinvesting… a board with no idea what to do next."

items.q: What is Sophie's main advice to the new board member?
options: Vote for the most profitable-looking company
Trust the P&L above all other documents
Wait for the next quarterly report before deciding
Ask structural questions the surface numbers cannot answer
items.why: Inferência: "ask me the structural questions… The numbers on the surface will never tell you that."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The balance sheet is a picture of the company's strategic position at a single moment." Strategic position refers to…
options: the physical location of the head office
the seniority of the finance director
where the business stands as a result of years of decisions
the target set for next quarter
items.why: Strategic position = posição estratégica: onde a empresa está em função das escolhas acumuladas.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Most of its equity is ___ — profit kept in the business rather than paid out."
options: a liability
a snapshot
retained earnings
fresh capital
items.why: Retained earnings = lucros retidos: o lucro reinvestido em vez de distribuído.

items.q: "The owners had to inject fresh capital to keep the company solvent." Fresh capital means…
options: profit generated during the year
new money put in from outside the business
a short-term bank loan repaid early
cash held in reserve
items.why: Fresh capital = capital novo aportado, distinto do lucro gerado internamente.

items.q: "The figures point to the quiet health of the business beneath the headlines." Quiet health describes…
options: publicity the company avoids
the wellbeing of the staff
a period of low trading activity
the underlying soundness not visible in the loud numbers
items.why: Quiet health = saúde silenciosa: a solidez de fundo que não aparece nas manchetes.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "How ___ the assets are determines how quickly they can be turned into cash."
options: strategic
structural
liquid
revealing
items.why: Liquid = líquido: o quão fácil é converter o ativo em caixa.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em conversas de finanças e conselho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the annual accounts." To sign off on means to…
options: postpone indefinitely
formally approve
comment informally
audit line by line
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on the plan to take on more short-term debt." They…
options: rewrote the whole plan
forgot to read it
resisted or challenged it
signed it immediately
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar, sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Cosmetic accounting changes will not move the needle on the company's real position." This means they will…
options: not make a meaningful difference
improve morale
take too long to calculate
attract regulatory attention
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.

items.q: "They promised to strengthen the balance sheet but never followed through." They…
options: delegated it to auditors
documented it badly
failed to carry it to completion
changed the target midway
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi prometido.

items.q: "The fresh capital gave the firm just enough room to stay afloat." To stay afloat means to…
options: repay all its debt at once
grow aggressively
avoid insolvency and keep operating
list on the stock exchange
items.why: Stay afloat = manter-se solvente, não afundar — sobreviver financeiramente.
